title: Jibril — the Trustworthy Spirit
subtitle: The angel who carried every word of the final revelation
sources: Qur'an 2:97 — 'it is [none but] he who has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart'
Qur'an 26:193-194 — 'The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down Upon your heart'
Sahih Muslim 8 — the hadith of Jibril in human form
Qur'an 96:1 — the night of Hira

chapters.heading: Iqra
chapters.body: He came to a man in a cave and said one word that rebuilt the world: Iqra — Read (96:1). The Qur'an names him Ruh al-Amin, the Trustworthy Spirit, and says of the revelation: 'The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down Upon your heart, [O Muhammad] - that you may be of the warners' (26:193-194). The Prophet ﷺ saw him in his true form, with six hundred wings that filled the horizon (Bukhari 3232). And he came disguised as a man in spotless clothes, with dark hair, sitting among the companions, resting his hands on his thighs — to ask about Islam, iman, and ihsan, so the Prophet ﷺ could teach the religion through his questions (Muslim 8). The greatest teacher in the ummah's history is an angel who asked the right questions. Every word of the Qur'an, every verse recited tonight anywhere on earth, traveled to humanity through him.

familyQuestion: Jibril asked questions so the companions could learn. What question could you ask tonight that would teach your whole family?

title: Mika'il — the Angel of Provision
subtitle: The one by whose hand the rain falls and the crops rise
sources: Qur'an 2:98 — named with Jibril as an angel of Allah

chapters.heading: Named in the Qur'an
chapters.body: Mika'il is named in the Qur'an beside Jibril (2:98), and his charge is the provision of the worlds: the rain that falls, the seeds that split, the harvest that feeds a planet. Beyond his name, the Qur'an says little about him. The common description of his charge as rain and provision comes from later tradition rather than from a verse, and this card does not present it as established. What stays certain is the lesson: provision is not only sent down from the sky; it is released by what the hand refuses to take.

familyQuestion: Provision itself rejoiced over one act of mercy. What is your hand holding that it should release this week?

title: Israfil — the Trumpet
subtitle: The horn is raised to his lips; the wait itself is mercy
sources: Qur'an 39:68 — 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills'
Qur'an 39:69 — the earth will shine with the light of its Lord
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2431 — 'the one with the horn' awaiting the command (hasan per al-Tirmidhi and Darussalam)

chapters.heading: The Longest Silence in Creation
chapters.body: The Qur'an describes the moment the Horn is blown: 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on' (39:68). The Prophet ﷺ said: how can I be at ease while the one with the horn has put the horn to his lips, listening for the command to blow? And he taught the Companions, when it weighed on them, to say: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs (Tirmidhi 2431, hasan per al-Tirmidhi and Darussalam). That hadith says 'the one with the horn' and does not name him; the scholars' naming of him as Israfil is not checked here. Think about what the wait means. The blast has not yet sounded; every day that passes is a day in which turning back is still open to you (a reflection, not a report). The Qur'an says that on that Day the earth will shine with the light of its Lord and the record will be placed (39:69). The scariest sound in existence has not yet sounded.

familyQuestion: Israfil's blast is delayed so you can repent. If today were the last day of the delay, what would you fix tonight?

title: Malak al-Mawt — the Angel of Death
subtitle: 'He has been entrusted with you' — and his door is always open
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — 'Say, The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you'
Qur'an 16:32 — the angels take the righteous saying 'Peace be upon you'
Qur'an 8:50 — the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved
Sahih al-Bukhari 6507 — the believer given glad tidings at death and longing to meet Allah

chapters.heading: The Gentle Taking
chapters.body: The Qur'an answers the question no one can escape: 'Say, The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you. Then to your Lord you will be returned' (32:11). Entrusted with you: the taking of your soul is a duty given to the angel by Allah. The Qur'an says the angels take the righteous saying: 'Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do' (16:32). And a hadith says that when death comes the believer is given news of Allah's pleasure and honour, and so longs to meet Him, while the disbeliever is given news of punishment and dreads the meeting (Bukhari 6507). The taking of those who disbelieved is described very differently: the angels strike their faces and their backs (8:50). Same door, two weathers — the difference is not the angel; it is the soul he is asked to carry.

familyQuestion: The Qur'an calls death a 'return' and a 'trust.' What would you want the record of your trust to say when it is handed over?

title: The Scribes on Your Shoulders
subtitle: Noble recorders, knowing whatever you do — writing right now
sources: Qur'an 82:10-12 — 'Noble and recording; They know whatever you do'
Qur'an 50:17-18 — 'when the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left'

chapters.heading: The Two Receivers
chapters.body: 'Man does not utter any word except that with him is an observer prepared' (50:18). The Qur'an gives them their posts: two angels, one on the right shoulder recording the good, one on the left recording the evil — and the hadith says that when a servant intends a bad deed it is not written until he does it, and if he leaves it for Allah's sake it is written as a good deed (Muslim 131). Read that again: mercy is written over your hesitation. The record begins with action, and mercy writes over intention. At the end, the book is presented: 'Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant' (17:14). The most quietly motivating sentence in the app: nothing you have ever done is missing from the record — and nothing you almost did is held against you.

familyQuestion: The pen waits during your hesitation. What deed are you hesitating on right now — good or bad?

title: Munkar & Nakir — the Two Questioners
subtitle: The three questions of the grave — told to prepare, never to terrorize
sources: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1071 — the three questions (hasan per Darussalam)
Qur'an 14:27 — 'Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter'
Sunan Abi Dawud 4753 — the longer report of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (sahih per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: Man Rabbuka?
chapters.body: When the believer is placed in the grave, the hadith teaches, two angels come to him and ask three questions: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is this man who was sent among you? (Tirmidhi 1071, hasan per Darussalam). The servant who answered honestly in life answers in the grave: My Lord is Allah; my religion is Islam; that is the Messenger of Allah — and, in the longer report of al-Bara' (Abu Dawud 4753 — sahih per al-Albani), a caller from the heavens confirms: My servant has spoken truth; the grave is widened as far as the eye can see, and a door to Paradise is opened to him. The design rule this library keeps: the grave is told to prepare, never to terrorize — the card ends where the Qur'an ends, at the firm word that holds a person steady: 'Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter' (14:27). The answers are learned in the living room, not in the grave.

familyQuestion: The three questions are about knowing, not performance. Could you answer all three tonight, out loud, in one sentence each?

title: The Angels You Never See
subtitle: The qarin, the dhikr circles' witnesses, and the ameen of heaven
sources: Sahih Muslim 2814 — every person has an assigned companion from the jinn; the Prophet's ﷺ companion urges only good
Sahih al-Bukhari 6408 — the angels who seek circles of dhikr and surround them with their wings
Sahih Muslim 2732 — the angel who answers your dua for your absent brother
Sunan an-Nasa'i 1282 — angels who convey the greetings of the ummah to the Prophet ﷺ (sahih per Darussalam)

chapters.heading: The Sky Fills Up
chapters.body: When people sit remembering Allah, the hadith says that angels who roam the roads looking for such gatherings call to one another, surround the people with their wings up to the lowest heaven, and Allah asks the angels about them, and says: I make you witnesses that I have forgiven them (Bukhari 6408). The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah has angels who travel the earth and convey to him the greetings of his ummah (Nasa'i 1282, graded sahih by Darussalam). When you make dua for your brother in his absence, an angel responds: the same be for you too (Muslim 2732). And the Prophet ﷺ said that every person has a companion from the jinn, and when the Companions asked if that applied to him, he said yes, but Allah helped him against it, so it urges him only to good (Muslim 2814). You are never as alone in a room as it feels.

familyQuestion: A gathering of dhikr fills the sky with witnesses. When did you last sit with people remembering Allah — and could you this week?

title: The Bearers of the Throne & the Seventy Wings
subtitle: Eight will bear it on the Day when the whole earth is in His grip
sources: Qur'an 69:17 — 'And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them'
Qur'an 39:75 and 40:7 — the angels around the Throne, and those who bear it, glorify their Lord
Sahih al-Bukhari 3232 — Jibril's six hundred wings

chapters.heading: The Size of the Unseen
chapters.body: Ibn Mas'ud reported that the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril with six hundred wings (Bukhari 3232); further scenery sometimes told of that sighting is not in the report and is not repeated here. The Day will summon the greatest of them: 'And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them, that Day, eight [of them]' (69:17) — eight, who on that Day will be as nothing in the grip of the One they carry. And the Qur'an adds the detail that steadies the heart: those who bear the Throne, and those around it, glorify their Lord with praise (39:75; 40:7). You can join that glorification at any moment. The largest beings in creation glorify Him in words you can also say.

familyQuestion: The throne-bearers recite a dua short enough for a child. When did you last say 'la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu' slowly, knowing who else is saying it?

title: Created from Smokeless Fire
subtitle: Before mankind, from fire — a civilization older than ours
sources: Qur'an 15:27 — 'the jinn We created before from scorching fire'
Qur'an 55:15 — 'He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire'

chapters.heading: An Older People
chapters.body: Long before Adam drew breath, another people walked the earth: 'And the jinn We created before from scorching fire' (15:27) — marij, the smokeless flame at the heart of a blaze. They are not ghosts, not demons by default, and not metaphors — the Qur'an treats them as a real created nation with faiths and accountability (72:11), like ours: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (51:56). Knowing they exist changes the weather of the night: you are not the only audience in the room, and the One who made both nations sees both at once. The app's rule is the Qur'an's rule: tell what is revealed, and let the rest stay veiled — their world is real, and it is not yours to explore.

familyQuestion: Allah made two nations to worship Him — ours and theirs. What does that tell you about how big the creation really is?

title: Iblis Refuses
subtitle: He was not an angel — and his argument is still in use
sources: Qur'an 2:34 — 'when We said to the angels, Prostrate before Adam; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused'
Qur'an 7:12 — 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay'

chapters.heading: I Am Better Than Him
chapters.body: The Qur'an is precise: Iblis was of the jinn (18:50), among those present when Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, and he refused — and his refusal had an argument: 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay' (7:12). Look at the anatomy of the fall: comparison, pride, and then the transfer of blame — 'because You have put me in error' (15:39), as if the One who commanded good had authored his disobedience. Allah answered the argument forever: 'Get out of it, for indeed you are expelled. And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense' (15:34-35). Every arrogance you have ever felt — I'm better than him, I deserve more than her — is that same sentence spoken in a smaller voice. The first sin in the universe was comparison.

familyQuestion: Iblis's fall began with comparing himself to someone. When did comparison last poison your contentment?

title: The Open Vow
subtitle: 'Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all'
sources: Qur'an 15:36-43 — 'he said: My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected'
Qur'an 7:16-17 — 'then I will come to them from before them and from behind them'

chapters.heading: Reprieved on Purpose
chapters.body: Iblis asked for time — not forgiveness: 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected' (15:36) — and Allah granted it, not as a favor but as a design: the trial of temptation now runs to the end of history. His strategy is mapped in the Qur'an: 'Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful' (7:17) — every direction except straight up, because nothing comes between the servant and his Lord except the servant's own turning. And note the promise within the threat: he said he would mislead “all” of them, and the Qur'an answers: 'Indeed, My servants - no authority will you have over them, except those who follow you of the deviators' (15:42). His reach has a border. The border is: those who do not follow.

familyQuestion: Shaytan was reprieved to test us — the test is the point. What is the hardest thing about being tested on purpose?

title: The Whisper — Waswas
subtitle: Not a command — a suggestion, thin as breath
sources: Qur'an 114:4-5 — 'From the evil of the retreating whisperer - Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind'
Qur'an 7:200 — 'and if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah'

chapters.heading: A Suggestion, Not a Voice
chapters.body: The Qur'an never has Shaytan forcing anyone. He whispers — waswas — 'who whispers into the breasts of mankind, from among the jinn and mankind' (114:5-6). Two sources of whisper: the jinn, and other people. The mechanics matter: a whisper needs a receiver, and the receiver has an answer prepared before the whisper arrives: 'And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing' (7:200). A familiar image compares it to a passing bird: it lands on your branch, it does not build a nest unless you let it stay. The Qur'an's instruction is to seek refuge in Allah (7:200), and the Prophet ﷺ taught that when a doubting whisper comes one should seek refuge in Allah and stop (Muslim 134). You cannot stop birds from flying over your head. You can stop them from nesting in your hair.

familyQuestion: The whisper only lands where it is welcomed. What branch of your life has a bird sitting on it right now?

title: Your Constant Companion
subtitle: Every soul has a jinn companion appointed
sources: Sahih Muslim 2814 — 'there is no one among you but he has been assigned a companion from the jinn... and an angel'

chapters.heading: The Jinn Beside You
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ taught what no eye can verify and every believer should know: each of you has a companion appointed from the jinn — a qarin — as you have one appointed from the angels. The companions asked: even you, O Messenger of Allah? — and he said: even me, except that Allah helped me against him, and he submitted (aslam), so he only commands me good (Muslim 2814). The hadith hands you two facts in one breath: the pressure is lifelong, and it is not unbeatable — the Prophet's own qarin submitted. The jinn companion whispers from within reach; the angel companion confirms truth. Your inner weather — whose voice feels closer tonight?

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ's qarin submitted. What would it take for your worst inner voice to stop having an audience?

title: Possession & the Evil Eye
subtitle: Real, rare, and never an excuse
sources: Qur'an 2:275 — 'those who consume interest... that is because they say: trade is like interest' — the context of affliction and cure
Sahih Muslim 2188 — the evil eye is real, and the Prophet ﷺ permitted ruqyah for it
Seerah and tafsir reports — the knots and the Mu'awwidhatan (not in Bukhari 3268; not checked here)

chapters.heading: Afflicted, and Still the Messenger
chapters.body: Sahih al-Bukhari 3268 (Aisha) reports that the Prophet ﷺ himself was bewitched, that Allah showed him the place of the spell, and that he was cured. Later reports add a knotted cord, eleven knots and the verses of the Mu'awwidhatan; those details come from tafsir and seerah reports, are not in Bukhari 3268, and were not checked here. If the best of creation could be afflicted and cured by revealed words, affliction is not disgrace — and the cure is not theater. But the balance the scholars insist on: possession and the evil eye are real (the evil eye is real, the Prophet ﷺ said — Muslim 2188 — and he permitted ruqyah for it — Tirmidhi 2059, sahih per Darussalam), and simultaneously they are rare, they are never an excuse for sin, and the first resort is always the same: the Qur'an itself. Ruqyah with al-Fatihah, the last two surahs, Ayat al-Kursi, and the morning and evening adhkar — this is the medicine, and it has no side effects.

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ was afflicted and cured by Qur'an. What affliction are you carrying that you haven't brought to the revealed words?

title: Sulayman's Jinn
subtitle: A kingdom of builders — and a lesson about borrowed power
sources: Qur'an 34:12-13; 21:82 — 'and of the devils were those who dived for him and did work other than that'
Qur'an 38:37-38 — 'every builder and diver And others bound together in shackles'

chapters.heading: Builders on a Leash
chapters.body: Allah subjected the jinn to Sulayman — not as magic, but as a granted kingdom: they built him lofty halls, statues, basins like reservoirs, and great fixed cauldrons (34:13); some dived for pearls, some labored; and the rebellious among them were kept 'bound together in shackles' (38:38). The Qur'an adds the detail that keeps the whole picture honest: 'And when We decreed for Solomon death, nothing indicated to the jinn his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff. But when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating punishment' (34:14). The jinn, working around the dead king, thought him alive by posture alone. Their knowledge failed at the one thing that mattered. Every power that serves you — wealth, health, people — is a staff held up by decree.

familyQuestion: Sulayman's jinn kept working, not knowing he had died. What are you serving that might not be holding the staff?

title: The Ifrit and the Throne of Bilqis
subtitle: One jinn's boast answered an hour's labor
sources: Qur'an 27:38-40 — 'A powerful one from among the jinn said, I will bring it to you before you rise from your place'

chapters.heading: I Will Bring It Before You Stand
chapters.body: When Bilqis, queen of Sheba, was being invited to Islam, Sulayman asked his council: which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission? 'A powerful one from among the jinn said, I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this [task] strong and trustworthy' (27:39). The throne — the seat of an empire, far away — arrived in the time it takes a man to blink... no: the ifrit promised it before Sulayman rose from his seat. Then the one 'who had knowledge of the Scripture' said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you — and it stood before Sulayman as if it had never moved (27:40). The jinn had power; the human had knowledge. The Qur'an honored both, but it gave the throne-bringing glory to the knowledge of one man with a Book — faster than a legion of ifrits. Your weapon is not hidden in the unseen; it is the revealed word you carry.

familyQuestion: The ifrit had power; the scholar had knowledge — and knowledge won. What knowledge are you neglecting that outranks every shortcut?

title: Jinn Who Heard the Qur'an
subtitle: A caravan of them, converted in one recitation
sources: Qur'an 72:1-2 — 'say: it has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said: indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an'
Qur'an 46:29-32 — 'when We directed to you a few of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an'
Sahih al-Bukhari 773 — Ibn Abbas: the jinn who heard the Fajr recitation at Nakhla

chapters.heading: The Jinn Who Listened
chapters.body: A company of jinn — the Qur'an tells their story in Surah al-Ahqaf and Surah al-Jinn — heard the recitation and went back to their people: 'O our people, indeed we have heard a [recited] Book revealed after Moses confirming what was before it which guides to the truth and to a straight path ... O our people, respond to the Messenger of Allah and believe in him' (46:30-31). Ibn Abbas reports (Bukhari 773) that the Prophet ﷺ set out with some companions toward the market of Ukaz; the jinn had been barred from the news of heaven, so they sent scouts in different directions, and one group found him at Nakhla leading the Fajr prayer. They listened to the Qur'an, returned to their people and said they had heard a guiding Qur'an and believed in it, and Surah al-Jinn was revealed: 'Say, [O Muhammad], It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an. It guides to the right course, and we have believed in it' (72:1-2). The unseen was listening, and some of it believed.

familyQuestion: Jinn converted by overhearing Fajr recitation. What does that say about what your own recitation could be doing unseen?

title: Jinn of the Masjid and the Graveyards
subtitle: Some believe, some guard, some flee from adhan
sources: Sahih Muslim 450 — the Prophet recited to the jinn; bones and dung are their provision
Sahih al-Bukhari 608 — Shaytan flees the adhan; Sahih al-Bukhari 3275 — the guardian from Allah for the one who recites Ayat al-Kursi

chapters.heading: The Mosque Is Shared
chapters.body: The hadith literature says that Shaytan flees when the adhan is called, passing wind so as not to hear it (Bukhari 608). They have their own food — bones and dung, the Prophet ﷺ said: do not use them for purification, for they are the provision of your brothers among the jinn (Muslim 450). The app keeps their stories in their place: real enough to respect, veiled enough to leave alone. The rule of this wing, as of the whole library: knowledge is protection, not a playground.

familyQuestion: The adhan drives them from the mosque. When you hear the adhan and keep sitting, who is more disciplined — you or them?

title: Why You Cannot See Them
subtitle: Veiled by design — and by mercy
sources: Qur'an 7:27 — 'he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them'
Qur'an 50:22 — 'You were certainly in unmindfulness of this, and We have removed from you your cover, so your sight, this Day, is sharp'

chapters.heading: One-Way Glass
chapters.body: The veil runs one direction: 'Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them' (7:27). They see you; you do not see them — and this asymmetry can be read as a mercy, not a deprivation: a world where the unseen were visible would be a world without rest, without privacy, without the freedom to struggle. The Qur'an promises the veil lifts exactly once: at death and resurrection, when the covering is removed — 'You were certainly in unmindfulness of this, and We have removed from you your cover, so your sight, this Day, is sharp' (50:22). Until then, the evidence is the Qur'an and the sound sunnah, and the demand is exactly what the demand would be if you could see: live as if watched — because you are.

familyQuestion: You are watched but not stalked — seen but given privacy. How would you live differently if the veil lifted for one day?

title: Protection from the Jinn
subtitle: The fortress is five sentences and a morning habit
sources: Qur'an 112, 113, 114 — the Mu'awwidhat and al-Ikhlas
Qur'an 2:255 — Ayat al-Kursi
Sahih al-Bukhari 3275 — Ayat al-Kursi before sleep: a guardian from Allah remains over you
Sahih Muslim 134 — refuge from Shaytan when the whisper comes

chapters.heading: The Fortress
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ never taught his companions to investigate the jinn — he taught them to be unreachable: Ayat al-Kursi before sleep, and a guardian from Allah stays with you through the night (Bukhari 3275). Al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas — the three quls — blown into the hands and wiped over the body, morning and evening (Abu Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani). Bismillah on entering and leaving. The Prophet ﷺ said: Shaytan attaches three knots at the back of your head at night, and on each knot he strikes: you have a long night ahead, so sleep — and if the servant wakes and remembers Allah, each knot is untied (Bukhari 1142). The whole system fits in five minutes. The fortress was never secrecy or fear. It was habit.

familyQuestion: The protection is five minutes of habit, not hours of fear. Which of the five are you missing most nights?

title: Play 1: Comparison
subtitle: He turns blessings into evidence against you
sources: Qur'an 20:122 — 'then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him' — Adam's response after sin
Qur'an 7:12 — Iblis's comparison: 'I am better than him'

chapters.heading: The Measuring Stick
chapters.body: Every human soul is, in the Qur'an's words, 'a persistent enjoiner of evil' (12:53), and Shaytan's oldest instrument against it is the measuring stick: look at their house, their waist, their followers, their ease. The Qur'an shows the antidote built into Adam's story — after the fall, he did not measure himself to the angels who had not sinned; he said: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and Allah 'turned to him in forgiveness and guided him' (20:122). Comparison was the devil's first word ('I am better than him' — 7:12) and gratitude is the answer to it. The counter-move is mechanical and immediate: the Prophet ﷺ taught that looking at those below you in provision — while looking at those above you in deen — steadies both contentment and ambition (Muslim 2963). You cannot stop the measuring stick from being shown to you. You can refuse to hold it.

familyQuestion: Comparison was the first word of the first devil. What are you measuring yourself against this week — and is it holding you or hurting you?

title: Play 2: Despair After Sin
subtitle: His only win is convincing you the door is locked
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — 'do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins'
Qur'an 12:87 — 'go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people'

chapters.heading: The Locked-Door Lie
chapters.body: No sin locks the door. The Qur'an addresses the sinner directly, in the second person, with the widest promise in scripture: 'Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful' (39:53) — all sins, to a people addressed as still His servants even in their transgression. Shaytan's play is to stand at the door after your fall and narrate: you knew better; you've gone too far; the prayer is pointless now. His goal is never the sin — you already committed it; his goal is the despair that stops the return. The evidence: Ya'qub, who lost two sons and a whole lifetime, told his children: 'go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people' (12:87) — he named despair itself the disbelief. The door has no lock on the inside.

familyQuestion: The widest promise in scripture is addressed to people in the middle of their sin. What door have you been treating as locked?

title: Play 3: The Delay Tactic
subtitle: He does not tell you 'no' — he tells you 'later'
sources: Qur'an 59:18-19 — 'And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves'
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2306 — hasten to good deeds before seven things (da'if per the English translation's label on sunnah.com; al-Tirmidhi's own grade was hasan gharib)

chapters.heading: Tomorrow's Trap
chapters.body: Shaytan rarely commands; he schedules. Not 'don't pray' — 'pray after this message.' Not 'don't repent' — 'repent when Ramadan comes.' (This is a reflection on the pattern, not a report.) The Qur'an names the danger of forgetting Allah in one breath: 'And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient' (59:19). The Prophet ﷺ urged haste: hasten to good deeds before seven things — poverty that overwhelms, wealth that distracts, illness that disables, old age that unsettles the mind, sudden death, the Dajjal, and the Hour (Tirmidhi 2306, da'if per the English translation's label on sunnah.com; al-Tirmidhi's own grade was hasan gharib). The counter-scheduling is to do the good deed immediately, small and now, before the whispers can open their calendar.

familyQuestion: He never says no — he says later. What is the one small good thing you could do in the next five minutes, ending one 'later' tonight?

title: Play 4: The Loop
subtitle: Shame feeds the sin that feeds the shame — break it with a sentence
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — the promise repeated over every returning sinner
Qur'an 2:286 — 'Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity'
Qur'an 3:135 — 'remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins'

chapters.heading: The Engine of Return
chapters.body: Secret sins run on an engine: sin, then shame, then the shame says you are the kind of person who sins, and that identity licenses the next sin — the loop closes itself. The devil does not need to tempt you each round; your shame does his work. The break is not willpower; it is a sentence said in the moment of shame — the Qur'an describes those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins (3:135). And the door of tawbah is not a yearly gate: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah accepts the servant's repentance until the soul reaches the throat (Tirmidhi 3537, hasan per Darussalam). The loop ends where it started: not with a perfect week, but with one turning — and the turning is available at 2am, mid-fall, mid-shame, every single time.

familyQuestion: The shame is not the punishment — it's the trap. What sentence could you say out loud tonight to break one loop?

title: Play 5: Anger & Argument
subtitle: He pours oil on every disagreement
sources: Qur'an 41:34 — 'And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6114 — 'the strong is not the one who overcomes people by wrestling; the strong is the one who controls himself in anger'

chapters.heading: The Oil
chapters.body: Shaytan is made from fire, and anger is his native element: a narration teaches that anger comes from the devil, who was created of fire (Abu Dawud 4784 — graded daʿif by al-Albani, so held lightly). His play in every argument is escalation — make him say the unforgivable thing, make her win at any cost, make the marriage, the friendship, the business partnership pay the price of one hot evening. The Prophet ﷺ taught the physical counter: if you stand, sit; if you are still angry, lie down (Abu Dawud 4782, sahih per al-Albani). The same weak narration adds wudu — water against fire — which many scholars still take as a fitting practice. And the moral counter is the verse he hates most: 'Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend' (41:34). He pours oil; you carry water. Every household learns which one wins.

familyQuestion: Water beats fire in this law. What is the 'sit down' or 'say something kinder' move in the argument you're in right now?

title: Play 6: Fame and the Hidden Sin
subtitle: He applauds your goodness when someone is watching
sources: Qur'an 107:4-6 — 'So woe to those who pray [But] who are heedless of their prayer - Those who make show [of their deeds]'
Sahih Muslim 1905 — the first three judged: the martyr, the reciter and the wealthy man who did it to be seen
Sahih al-Bukhari 660 — the seven shaded by Allah's shade; the hidden charity

chapters.heading: The Applause Trap
chapters.body: The hadith that should keep every visible believer awake: the first people judged on the Day are three — a martyr, a scholar and reciter of the Qur'an, and a wealthy man who spent. Each tells Allah what he did for Him, and Allah answers that he did it so that it would be said: a brave man, a scholar, a generous man — and it was said. Each is dragged on his face into the Fire (Muslim 1905, from Abu Hurayrah). The Qur'an speaks of those 'who make show [of their deeds]' (107:6). Shaytan's most sophisticated play is not moving you to sin — it is moving your worship toward the audience: the prayer shortened for the crowd, the sadaqah announced, the knowledge performed. The antidote is a hidden habit the size of a seed: the Prophet ﷺ said seven are shaded by Allah's shade on the Day when there is no shade but His — among them a man who gives charity so hidden that his left hand does not know what his right hand has given (Bukhari 660). Let some of your good be known only to the One who counts it.

familyQuestion: Three heroes of the world were told 'your wage was paid in applause.' What good thing could you do this week that no one but Allah will ever know about?

title: The Last Breath
subtitle: The shudder, the brightness, and the family left at the door
sources: Qur'an 50:19 — 'and the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid'
Sahih Muslim 927 — 'the deceased is punished because of his family's weeping over him' (scholars discuss its precise meaning)

chapters.heading: Sakarat
chapters.body: The Qur'an names the moment with one word: sakarat — the stupor of death — 'the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid' (50:19). In that clarity, the veils fall: wealth stops mattering, grievances resolve themselves, and the soul learns the geography it had ignored. The Prophet ﷺ taught the etiquette of the dying room: prompt the one leaving to say la ilaha illa Allah (Muslim 916); do not wail over the body — the Prophet ﷺ said 'the deceased is punished because of his family's weeping over him' (Muslim 927; scholars discuss exactly what this means, but the guidance to restrain wailing and meet grief with patience is clear); close the eyes, cover the body, hasten the burial. And to the family left at the door, three sentences: the Prophet ﷺ said — what reaches the deceased of his deeds is three: an ongoing charity, useful knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for him (Muslim 1631). The last breath is not the end of the relationship; it is a change of address. Three things keep the mail running.

familyQuestion: Three things reach the dead: charity, knowledge, a praying child. Which of the three are you building for your parents right now?

title: The Ascent of the Soul
subtitle: Gates of heaven that open — and a grave that calls it home
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — 'The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you'
Qur'an 3:169-170 — those killed in the cause of Allah are alive with their Lord
Sahih Muslim 1887 — the souls of the martyrs in green birds beneath the Throne's lamps
Sahih al-Bukhari 6507 — the believer's glad tidings at death

chapters.heading: Carried Upward
chapters.body: The Qur'an says the angels take the righteous saying: 'Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do' (16:32), and a hadith says the believer is given news of Allah's pleasure and honour when death comes, and longs to meet Him (Bukhari 6507). The soul of the martyr is described even more specifically: Ibn Mas'ud relayed from the Prophet ﷺ that the souls of the martyrs are in green birds, which nest in lamps hung beneath the Throne and eat the fruits of Paradise wherever they wish (Muslim 1887); and the Qur'an speaks of those killed in Allah's cause as alive with their Lord, receiving provision and rejoicing (3:169-170). But the road runs both ways: the Qur'an speaks of the day 'the contents of the graves are scattered' (100:9), and every soul will be raised. The journey has a direction for every soul; the only open question is the address.

familyQuestion: The soul is 'carried' — never abandoned mid-journey. Who in your life needs carrying right now, and are you doing it?

title: The Grave — Its Blessings
subtitle: A garden of the Paradise — or a pit of the Fire
sources: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 2460 — 'the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire' (daʿif per Darussalam; wording held lightly)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1379 · Sahih Muslim 2866 — the deceased is shown his place morning and evening
Sunan Abi Dawud 4753 — the grave widened as far as the eye can see (al-Bara' ibn 'Azib; sahih per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: Widened as Far as the Eye Can See
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ is reported to have given the grave its two weathers in one sentence: 'the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire' (Tirmidhi 2460, daif per Darussalam — a weak chain, so hold the wording lightly). What is firmly established is that the deceased is shown his place every morning and evening (Bukhari 1379, Muslim 2866), and that for the believer the grave is widened as far as his eye can see and a door to Paradise is opened (Abu Dawud 4753, sahih per al-Albani). In the longer report of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib in Musnad Ahmad (number and grade not checked here), a man of handsome face, fine clothes, and pleasant fragrance comes to him and says: rejoice in what pleases you — and he is the servant's own righteous deeds, walking to meet him as a person. The grave is not a waiting room to be feared; for the one who sent good deeds ahead, it is the first hotel of the journey — and the caller at its door is the best version of everything he ever did.

familyQuestion: Your deeds come to meet you as a person. What kind of 'person' are you sending ahead of yourself?

title: Barzakh — The Barrier
subtitle: A barrier between two worlds
sources: Qur'an 23:99-100 — 'until, when death comes to one of them, he says, My Lord, send me back That I might do righteousness in that which I left behind'
Qur'an 36:51-52 — the blast that wakes the sleepers of the centuries

chapters.heading: The Waiting Place
chapters.body: The Qur'an names the interval: barzakh — a barrier behind which nothing returns: 'and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected' (23:100). The sleeper does not experience the centuries. The Qur'an describes the waking: the horn is blown, and the sleepers rise and ask who has raised them from their sleeping place (36:51-52). Reports in the hadith literature speak of the grave as the first station of the Hereafter (collection and grading not checked here). How the interval is experienced is among the matters of the unseen on which the sources say little. As a reflection: the barzakh can be read as the mercy of a pause, between the address the soul left and the address it is going to.

familyQuestion: The barzakh is a rest between two journeys. If tonight's sleep were your last, which loose ends would you regret not tying?

title: The Trial of the Grave — and Its Shields
subtitle: Real, rare, and bounded by the morning adhkar
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1374 — the grave's questioning, the believer's seat in Paradise and the hammers
Sahih Muslim 1913 — the one who guards the frontier is kept safe from the tester of the grave
Qur'an 40:45-46 — 'they are exposed to it morning and evening' for Pharaoh's people

chapters.heading: The Trial and the Shields
chapters.body: The trial of the grave is established — the hadith of the two angels who sit the deceased up after the companions leave and ask what he used to say about this man, Muhammad ﷺ; the believer testifies that he is Allah's slave and messenger and is shown his seat in the Fire replaced by a seat in Paradise, while the hypocrite or disbeliever says 'I do not know; I used to say what the people said' and is struck with iron hammers (Bukhari 1374). But the tradition is equally firm that there is protection: the Prophet ﷺ said that one who guards the frontier for a day and night, and dies, has his deeds continue to be credited to him, his provision continues, and he is kept safe from the tester, which the translation renders as the torment of the grave (Muslim 1913, from Salman). The Qur'an describes the people of Pharaoh as exposed to the Fire 'morning and evening' before the Day the Hour appears (40:46). The app tells this plainly and stops where the sources stop: the trial is real; the shields are named; the believer's duty is to prepare, not to speculate.

familyQuestion: The shields are named and take five minutes. What is your morning adhkar actually like — armor, or afterthought?

title: The First Blast
subtitle: The end of the old world's tenancy
sources: Qur'an 39:68 — 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills'
Qur'an 27:87 — 'and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills'
Sahih al-Bukhari 4814 — 'forty' between the two blasts; Abu Hurayrah declined to say days, months or years

chapters.heading: The Silence Between the Blasts
chapters.body: The Qur'an describes the scene: the whole earth will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection and 'the heavens will be folded in His right hand' (39:67). Then: 'whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills' (39:68). The Prophet ﷺ said there will be forty between the two blowings; Abu Hurayrah was asked whether he meant forty days, forty years or forty months, and he declined to say (Bukhari 4814). The old world's tenancy ends in one sound. The Qur'an promised it would; the universe keeps the appointment.

familyQuestion: One sound ends everything. If the appointment is certain, what deserves your worry — the sound, or what you send ahead of it?

title: The Second Blast
subtitle: Standing barefoot on a changed earth, facing the Lord of the worlds
sources: Qur'an 36:51-52 — 'And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten'
Qur'an 18:47 — the mountains removed, the earth prominent
Qur'an 14:48 — 'the day the earth will be replaced by another earth'
Qur'an 70:4 and 22:2
Sahih Muslim 2790 — the earth like a white loaf of bread
Sahih al-Bukhari 6524 — gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised
Sahih al-Bukhari 6522 — the groups at the gathering
Sahih al-Bukhari 6532 — the sweat on the Day of Resurrection

chapters.heading: At Once They Rise
chapters.body: The second blast is the waking: 'And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place? [The reply will be], This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth' (36:51-52). The earth itself is replaced (14:48) and the mountains removed (18:47); the Prophet ﷺ described the people gathered on a pale plain like a white loaf of bread, with no landmark for anyone (Muslim 2790, from Sahl ibn Sa'd), and said that people will meet Allah barefoot, naked and uncircumcised (Bukhari 6524, from Ibn Abbas) — a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years (70:4). And the Qur'an records the detail that steadies every heart: 'On the Day you see it every nursing mother will be distracted from that [child] she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people [appearing] intoxicated while they are not intoxicated; but the punishment of Allah is severe' (22:2). No one will have time for anyone but themselves — and yet: Abu Hurayrah reports that the gathering has groups: some hoping and fearing, some riding two, three or ten to a camel, and the rest driven toward the Fire (Bukhari 6522); and that on that Day people will sweat until it reaches their mouths and ears (Bukhari 6532). The rising is certain; the shade is the variable.

familyQuestion: On that day no one will look at anyone else. Who are you relying on besides yourself — and have you thanked them?

title: The Scales
subtitle: A grain of mustard's weight of good will be seen
sources: Qur'an 101:6-8 — 'then as for one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life'
Qur'an 99:7-8 — 'whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it'

chapters.heading: An Atom's Weight
chapters.body: The scales are the most democratic institution in existence: 'And the weighing [of deeds] that Day will be the truth. So those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful. And those whose scales are light - they are the ones who will lose themselves for what injustice they were doing toward Our verses' (7:8-9). No advocate speaks there; the deeds themselves testify — hands, feet, and skin will bear witness against their owner (36:65). But read the mercy folded into the precision: 'whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' (99:7-8). An atom. The smallest kindness — the water given to a dog, the thorn removed from the road, the cup passed to a stranger — weighs. The Prophet ﷺ said no fatigue, nor disease, nor sorrow, nor harm befalls a Muslim except that Allah expiates by it, even a thorn (Bukhari 5641). Nothing is wasted; nothing is lost; the scale has no rounding error.

familyQuestion: An atom's weight will be seen. What tiny good have you been treating as too small to matter?

title: The Bridge
subtitle: Everyone crosses; what differs is the light and the grip
sources: Qur'an 19:71 — 'And there is none of you except he will come to it'
Qur'an 19:72 and 57:12 — the saved, and the believers' light
Sahih Muslim 183 — the bridge, the crossing, the believers' plea

chapters.heading: Thinner Than a Hair
chapters.body: The Qur'an makes the bridge universal — a passage no soul skips: 'And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed' (19:71). The hadith gives its dimensions: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said, 'I have come to know that the bridge would be thinner even than the hair and sharper than the sword' (Muslim 183 — his own statement), and in the report he gives, the bridge over Hell has hooks, tongs and thorns, and the believers cross it at different speeds: in the twinkling of an eye, like lightning, like wind, while some are pulled into the Fire. But the verse that follows in the Qur'an is the one that answers it: 'Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees' (19:72). Salvation is not the avoidance of the bridge; it is what crosses with you. The Qur'an gives the believers a light for that Day: 'their light proceeding before them and on their right' (57:12). And when the believers have crossed, they plead for brothers who fasted and prayed and performed pilgrimage with them, and Allah takes a handful who never did good and casts them into the river of life (Muslim 183).

familyQuestion: Even a spark on the big toe crosses. What is your light made of right now — what deeds are fueling it?

title: Why did Allah create me?
subtitle: The question beneath every other question
sources: Qur'an 51:56 — 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me'
Qur'an 67:2 — 'He who created death and life to test you'
Sahih Muslim 2865 — people created with a natural inclination to worship Allah; the devils led them away

chapters.heading: The Straight Answer
chapters.body: The Qur'an answers without poetry, which is its mercy: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (51:56). Worship here can be read as wider than ritual alone — knowing Him, relying on Him, choosing Him when choice costs (a reflection this card offers, not a quotation). The test-frame comes elsewhere in revelation: '[He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed' (67:2) — life is the examination hall, not the playground and not the prison. You were made on purpose, for a purpose: the Prophet ﷺ relayed what his Lord taught him, that people were created with a natural inclination to worship Allah, and the devils came to them and led them away from their religion (Muslim 2865, the sermon of Iyad ibn Himar). The 2am answer is one sentence: you were made to know and serve your Maker, and every gift in your life is a question about how you spent it.

familyQuestion: If life is a test, which question are you currently failing on purpose?

title: What happens when I die?
subtitle: The question the app was named after
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — the entrusted taking
Qur'an 23:100 — the barrier
Qur'an 36:51-52 — the waking

chapters.heading: The Road in Four Stops
chapters.body: The road has four stops, and the Qur'an gives each one: the taking — 'The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you' (32:11); the waiting — the grave and its barzakh, 'a barrier until the Day they are resurrected' (23:100); the waking — 'the horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten' (36:51); and the meeting — 'that day you will be exhibited; not hidden among you is anything concealed' (69:18). Nothing in the four stops is speculation: every stage has a verse. The 2am fear of death is, at bottom, fear of the unknown — and the cure for fear of the unknown is the map. You are not traveling an unmarked road; the whole journey is described by the One who built it. The only open question the map leaves is the condition of the traveler.

familyQuestion: The map exists. What is the condition of the traveler tonight — prepared, or postponing?

title: Where is Allah?
subtitle: Above the Throne — and nearer than the jugular
sources: Qur'an 20:5 — 'The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established'
Qur'an 50:16 — 'We are closer to him than his jugular vein'
Qur'an 40:7 and 69:17 — the angels who carry the Throne
Sahih Muslim 537 — the slave-girl of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam: 'Where is Allah?'

chapters.heading: Both Directions at Once
chapters.body: The Qur'an holds two truths the mind cannot fuse and never asks it to: Allah is above the Throne — 'The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established' (20:5) — the Throne the Qur'an says angels carry (40:7, 69:17); and He is nearer than the jugular — 'We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein' (50:16) — closer than the blood in your neck at this moment. The tradition guards both from distortion: the Prophet ﷺ asked the slave-girl of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam 'where is Allah?' and she answered: in the heaven; he asked who he was and she said: you are the Messenger of Allah; and he said: free her, for she is a believing woman (Muslim 537). Up is direction; near is presence. The 2am comfort is the combination: you are small beneath a vast Throne — and you are never, for one second, unsupervised in the dark. Both are mercy. Scholars have understood 'above the Throne' (istiwa) in different ways — some affirm it as it came and leave its manner to Allah, others interpret it figuratively; this card follows the wording of the verses and takes no side, and the question is for a scholar.

familyQuestion: Above the Throne and nearer than your neck — which side of that truth do you feel more tonight?

title: Are the jinn in this room with me right now?
subtitle: Yes — and it changes nothing you need to do
sources: Qur'an 72:6 — 'And there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn'
Sahih Muslim 2814 — the appointed companions
Sunan Abi Dawud 5082 (hasan per al-Albani) — the evening shield of the three quls

chapters.heading: Occupied, Always
chapters.body: The honest answer: every soul walks with an appointed companion from the jinn and one from the angels (Muslim 2814), and jinn inhabit the places people abandon — ruins, deserts, the emptiness between houses (a common teaching; no report was checked for it here). So yes: you are sharing the planet, and at moments the room. Now the question the question is really asking — 'am I in danger?' — and the revealed answer is the shield: the three quls morning and evening, Ayat al-Kursi at night, bismillah on entering. The Prophet ﷺ did not teach his companions to detect jinn; he taught them to be unreachable by habit (Abu Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani). A believer who keeps the shields is the boringest address in the unseen world: nothing to answer, nothing to open, nothing to follow. You are never alone — and you were never told to be afraid of your roommate.

familyQuestion: You share every room. What would change in your private habits if you truly believed you have company?

title: Will Allah forgive my worst sin?
subtitle: The list of the unforgiven is shorter than your fear
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — 'Allah forgives all sins'
Qur'an 4:48 — 'Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills'
Qur'an 25:68-70 — 'And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity ... those who repent'

chapters.heading: The Short List
chapters.body: The Qur'an is blunt about the one wall: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (4:48) — shirk dies only by repentance, and repentance from shirk is accepted: 'Say to those who have disbelieved [that] if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven for them' (8:38). The even harder case the Qur'an names directly: those who never invoked another god, nor killed a soul forbidden by Allah, nor committed adultery — 'Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful' (25:68-70). Murder and zina — replaced with good deeds for the one who turns. The Prophet ﷺ told the man who killed ninety-nine people and asked if repentance remained for him: yes (Bukhari 3470). Your worst sin has a precedent of forgiveness larger than it. The only sin that cannot be forgiven is the one you refuse to bring.

familyQuestion: The wall is one: refusing to turn. What are you refusing to bring to the door?

title: Why do bad things happen to good people?
subtitle: The question of the test — and of meanings deferred
sources: Qur'an 2:286 — 'Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity'
Qur'an 67:2 — the test
Qur'an 39:53 — mercy
Sahih Muslim 2999 — 'amazing is the affair of the believer'

chapters.heading: The Answer That Isn't an Explanation
chapters.body: The Qur'an's answer is not a philosophy of evil; it is a promise inside a test: life is '[He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed' (67:2), and no burden exceeds the strength lent with it (2:286). The Prophet ﷺ gave the shape of the answer: 'Amazing is the affair of the believer — all of it is good for him, and that is for no one but the believer: if prosperity reaches him he is grateful, and that is good for him; if harm reaches him he is patient, and that is good for him' (Muslim 2999). Gratitude and patience: the two doors by which every event enters as good. And under it all sits a Qur'anic teaching this card names, in its own framing, 'deferred interpretation': 'Perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good' (4:19), and the verse the angels themselves answered with at the creation of Adam: 'They said, Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You? Allah said, Indeed, I know that which you do not know' (2:30). The meaning of events is written; the ink is still wet. Wait for the Author to finish the sentence.

familyQuestion: 'I know that which you do not know.' What event in your life are you judging before the Author finished the sentence?

title: Are the end times near?
subtitle: Every generation is closer than the last — the signs are a syllabus, not a date
sources: Qur'an 33:63 — 'People ask you concerning the Hour. Say, Knowledge of it is only with Allah'
Qur'an 47:18 — 'Then do they await except that the Hour should come upon them unexpectedly?'
Sahih al-Bukhari 80 — knowledge lifted, ignorance, wine, zina
Sahih al-Bukhari 7121 — time passing quickly, trials and killing, abundant wealth
Sahih Muslim 8 — barefoot goat-herds competing in tall buildings

chapters.heading: Closer Every Day
chapters.body: The signs of the Hour are not a date but a syllabus. The Prophet ﷺ listed signs: knowledge would be lifted, ignorance would spread, wine would be drunk widely, and illicit relations become open (Bukhari 80); time would seem to pass quickly, knowledge would diminish, trials and killing would spread, and wealth would grow so abundant that a rich man would struggle to find anyone to accept his charity (Bukhari 7121); and, in the hadith of Jibril, that barefoot, destitute goat-herds would compete in constructing magnificent buildings (Muslim 8). These were named fourteen centuries ago and read like a checklist only to those who miss the point. The Qur'an's instruction is precise: 'They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him' (7:187). The signs are not a date; they are a list of things to guard against and prepare for, issued by the One who knows the date. The wise use signs the way travelers use milestones: not to argue about the miles, but to check the fuel.

familyQuestion: The signs are a syllabus. Which line of that syllabus is your own household failing right now?

title: Who is the Mahdi? Will Isa really return?
subtitle: Yes — as Allah's servant and the Prophet's ﷺ brother
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 2476 — the descent of Isa, breaking the cross, killing the swine, ruling by the Qur'an
Sunan Abi Dawud 4282 — the hadith of the Mahdi (hasan sahih per al-Albani; some scholars dispute it)
Qur'an 4:157-158 — 'rather, Allah raised him to Himself'

chapters.heading: The Return That Is Not a Sequel
chapters.body: The hadith is emphatic and its details are famous: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, the son of Maryam will soon descend among you as a just judge, and he will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and wealth will flow until no one takes it' (Bukhari 2476). The same narration anchors the essential correction: Isa returns ruling by this Qur'an as a Muslim among Muslims, not with a new book. The long hadith of al-Nawwas in Sahih Muslim 2937 adds that he descends at the white minaret in the east of Damascus and that the Dajjal is killed by him; the reports speak of a leader of the Muslims at that time, and scholars differ on whether and how that leader is the Mahdi. As for the Mahdi: the Prophet ﷺ said the earth will be filled with injustice and then a man from his household will come and fill it with justice, ruling seven years (Abu Dawud 4282, hasan sahih per al-Albani; some scholars dispute it). The app's rule on this wing is the scholars' rule: believe the return, reject every date-setter, and leave the schedule with the One who kept it (33:63). The future of this faith is not a mystery novel. It is a promise with a seal on it.

familyQuestion: Isa returns to rule by the Qur'an. What does that tell you about which book outranks every other book on earth?

title: Who is the Dajjal?
subtitle: The greatest trial in human history — and every prophet warned his nation
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3337 — no prophet but warned his nation of the Dajjal; he is one-eyed
Sahih Muslim 2933 — the letters k-f-r between the Dajjal's eyes
Sahih Muslim 809 — the first ten verses of Surah al-Kahf protect from the Dajjal
Sahih Muslim 2946 — no creation greater than the Dajjal since Adam
Sahih Muslim 2937 — the report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an: the Dajjal and the descent of Isa

chapters.heading: One-Eyed
chapters.body: The hadith collections devote more space to the Dajjal than to almost any other end-time matter, and every generation has asked why: because, the Prophet ﷺ said in a public address, there was no prophet but warned his nation against him — Nuh and the prophets after him (Bukhari 3337, from Ibn Umar); and he added something no earlier prophet had told their people: the Dajjal is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed (Bukhari 3337). Another report adds that the letters k-f-r are written between his eyes (Muslim 2933, from Anas). The Prophet's counsel is detailed: whoever memorizes the first ten verses of Surah al-Kahf is protected from the Dajjal (Muslim 809, from Abu al-Darda). The famous hadith makes the scale of the trial personal: from the creation of Adam until the Last Hour there is no creation that causes more trouble than the Dajjal (Muslim 2946, from Imran ibn Husayn). And the long report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an tells of the Dajjal and then the descent of Isa (Muslim 2937). The greatest trial in history is a trial the Prophet ﷺ taught his community to prepare for.

familyQuestion: Every prophet warned of him, and the exit is ten verses. When did you last read al-Kahf's opening?

title: Who are Ya'juj and Ma'juj?
subtitle: The nations behind the barrier — released when the promise arrives
sources: Qur'an 18:94-98 — Dhul-Qarnayn builds the barrier
Qur'an 21:96 — 'Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend'

chapters.heading: The Iron and Copper Wall
chapters.body: The Qur'an tells their whole known story in Surah al-Kahf: a people beyond the known world, devastating every people they pass, petitioning Dhul-Qarnayn (whose identity the sources dispute; see his own story) — 'So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier' (18:94). He refused payment and used their own materials: 'bring me sheets of iron' — until, when the gap between the two mountains was leveled, he said: blow — until, when he had made it fire, he said: bring me molten copper to pour over it — and they could neither scale it nor pierce it (18:96-97). Then came the sentence the believers repeat daily in Surah al-Kahf: '[Dhul-Qarnayn] said, This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true' (18:98). Every recitation of al-Kahf renews the witness: the barrier stands by decree, the release is scheduled, and the promise — like everything in this wing — has never once failed.

familyQuestion: The barrier stands by decree, not by iron. What barrier in your life is actually being held up by a promise?

title: Will I be alone when I die?
subtitle: The only genuinely lonely thing is dying without the One
sources: Qur'an 35:18 — 'And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry some of] its load'
Qur'an 50:19 — the truth arrives with the stupor
Qur'an 6:164 and 16:128
Sahih al-Bukhari 6507 — the believer's glad tidings at death
'Die before you die' — a saying often quoted; not shown here to be an authentic hadith (no collection or number was found)

chapters.heading: The Room Empties, the Throne Stays
chapters.body: Alone is the wrong word, and the Qur'an corrects it in both directions: 'every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another' (6:164); the solitude of dying is absolute and shared by every human who ever lived (a reflection: no one can die your death or say your la ilaha illa Allah for you). And simultaneously: 'Allah is with those who fear Him' (16:128), and a hadith says that when death comes the believer is given news of Allah's pleasure and honour and longs to meet Him (Bukhari 6507). 'Die before you die' is a saying often quoted, but it is not shown here to be an authentic hadith (no collection or number was found for it) — read it, if at all, as a reflection: practice the loneliness now, in prayer, in the night, in the quiet sitting after fajr — so that when the room empties for real, the emptiness is already familiar. You will not be alone with nothing; you will be, for the first time, alone with the One who was always there.

familyQuestion: 'Die before you die' — practice the loneliness. When did you last sit completely alone, on purpose, with no screen?

title: Will anyone intercede for me?
subtitle: Three rescues on a day with no other rescuer
sources: Qur'an 2:255 — 'who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?'
Qur'an 17:79 and 82:19
Sahih Muslim 193 — the Prophet's ﷺ intercession
Sunan Abi Dawud 2522 — the martyr's intercession for seventy of his family (sahih per al-Albani)
Sahih Muslim 183 — the believers plead for their brothers in the Fire
Sahih Muslim 2732 — dua for an absent brother
Qur'an 4:85 — 'Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a reward therefrom'

chapters.heading: The Three Doors
chapters.body: The hadith of the intercession is long, and its architecture is mercy: on a day when no soul can help another (82:19), people go to Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, and each declines, citing an error of his own; they come to Muhammad ﷺ, who says he will ask his Lord for permission, and he falls in prostration; when he is told, raise your head, O Muhammad, he praises his Lord with words he is taught, then intercedes; a limit is set, and he brings people out of the Fire into Paradise, and this happens several times (Muslim 193). The Qur'an promises that station: 'it is expected that your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station' (17:79). A second door: the Prophet ﷺ said a martyr's intercession will be accepted for seventy members of his family (Abu Dawud 2522, graded sahih by al-Albani). A third: the believers plead for brothers who were fasting and praying and performing pilgrimage with them, and are allowed to bring them out (Muslim 183). And the Qur'an opens the same word downward for you: 'Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a reward therefrom' (4:85) — intercession is not only for prophets. When you make dua for your brother in his absence, an angel says: the same be for you too (Muslim 2732).

familyQuestion: Intercession is a currency. What interceding are you doing now — teaching, praying, forgiving — that will speak for you then?

title: Is Hell forever?
subtitle: For those who choose it as home — yes; and the door out is before death
sources: Qur'an 4:56 — 'Every time their skins are roasted through We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment'
Qur'an 78:21-26 — 'An appropriate recompense'
Qur'an 2:167 — 'And they are never to emerge from the Fire'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6560 — those with a mustard seed of faith are brought out and sprout in the river al-Hayat
Sahih Muslim 183 — Allah takes out a handful and casts them into the river of life

chapters.heading: The Seriousness and the Door
chapters.body: The Qur'an is as serious about Hell as a doctor about cancer — not to relish the diagnosis but to make the cure unmissable. Its duration for the rejecters is stated without softening: 'And they are never to emerge from the Fire' (2:167); 'nor will it be permitted for them to make an excuse' (77:36). And the tradition adds that some who entered the Fire will be brought out of it: anyone with faith as small as a mustard seed will be taken out and placed in a river called al-Hayat, where they sprout like a seed on the bank of a flood stream (Bukhari 6560, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri), and in the long report of the Day of Resurrection Allah takes out a handful who never did good and casts them into the river of life (Muslim 183). The duration of the Fire has been discussed by scholars across the schools; this card follows the plain wording of the verses and leaves the discussion to a scholar. The forever belongs to the ones who treated the door as a wall while it stood open. The door's name is repentance, and its hours are the hours of your life. Everything in this app about Hell exists to make that door look the size it actually is.

familyQuestion: The door's hours are your hours. If the door had a closing time, what would you do before it?

title: What is Paradise actually like?
subtitle: No eye has seen it — which is the point
sources: Qur'an 32:17 — 'And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3244 — 'what no eye has seen and no ear has heard'
Qur'an 9:72 — 'gardens beneath which rivers flow'

chapters.heading: The Unseen Reward for the Unseen Deeds
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ said it in the hadith every Muslim knows: Allah has prepared for His righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to any heart (Bukhari 3244). The Qur'an's own description — 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' (9:72), rivers of milk and honey, spouses created anew, garments of silk and gold — is given in words of this world; the Prophet's ﷺ words that it holds what no eye has seen are the reminder that the description is not the thing (reading the descriptions as analogy is an interpretation, not a report). And the architecture of the reward mirrors the test: the people of the unseen are repaid in kind — 'And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do' (32:17). Hidden deeds, hidden reward. The night prayer no one saw, the charity no one knew, the tear at 2am wiped before anyone noticed — all of it compounds in a currency this world has never printed.

familyQuestion: Hidden deeds, hidden reward. What are you doing tonight that no eye will ever see?

title: Why do I have to pray five times a day?
subtitle: The appointment is the relationship
sources: Qur'an 20:14 — 'indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance'
Qur'an 29:45 — 'Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing'
Sahih Muslim 162 — the five prayers at the Night Journey; fifty reduced to five with the reward of fifty
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2621 — 'the covenant between us and them is the prayer' (hasan sahih gharib per al-Tirmidhi; sahih per Darussalam)
Sunan an-Nasa'i 463 — the same hadith (sahih per Darussalam)

chapters.heading: Five Appointments with the King
chapters.body: The five prayers were gifted at the summit of the heavens during the Night Journey — fifty first, then five with the reward of fifty (Muslim 162, from Anas; each prayer is credited as ten) — and the number is the design: a day cannot pass without the servant being called back. The Qur'an gives the mechanism: 'establish prayer for My remembrance' (20:14); and the effect: 'prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater' (29:45). The Prophet ﷺ drew the contract in one line: 'the covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved' (Tirmidhi 2621, hasan sahih gharib per al-Tirmidhi and sahih per Darussalam; also Nasa'i 463, sahih per Darussalam) — not because the King needs the audience, but because the servant unmade by distance is the one who stops coming. Five times a day is not a tax on your time. It is the only schedule in your life where Someone infinitely above you insists on seeing you anyway. Scholars differ on what the saying about abandoning the prayer means for one who neglects it through laziness rather than denial; that is a question for a scholar.

familyQuestion: The King calls five times and waits. When you delay the prayer, what are you telling the One who keeps the appointment?
